summary: The candidate is a partial fix. It corrects the divisible 42-token capture from eight unequal rows to seven uniform width-6 rows and fixes the independently reproduced DSV4 overlapping metadata-copy mechanism. It does not make Engram layout-aware: genuine compact-ragged tiers remain incompatible with the issue-described equal-block Engram contract, and the full DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash first-forward path was not run.

tests.what_was_measured: The actual base build_capture_verify_lens helper produced 42 tokens / 8 slots -> [6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5], matching the reported capture geometry. It also produced the recorded 41/43/47 boundary layouts. Evidence: raw/base-environment-and-repro.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: Base failure and candidate success for overlapping DSV4 metadata views ran on AMD Instinct MI355X tensors using PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015.
remaining_counterexamples: At width 6, 41 tokens use seven rows [6,6,6,6,6,6,5], violating the issue-described equal-block Engram contract.
At width 6, 43 tokens use eight rows [6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5], violating the issue-described equal-block Engram contract.
At width 6, 47 tokens use eight rows [6,6,6,6,6,6,6,5], violating the issue-described equal-block Engram contract.
No Engram implementation is present, so per-request hash context and numerical hash outputs cannot be compared with an independent reference.
The full first-forward path after capture was not run with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; only the isolated real-device DSV4 overlap mechanism was validated.
remaining_limitations: The checkout contains no EngramHasher, layers/engram.py, or DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram integration.
The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights and reported four-node NVIDIA GB10 TP4/EP4 CUDA deployment are unavailable on the assigned single AMD ROCm GPU.
CUDA graph capture and an end-to-end first request for the reported architecture remain unverified.
No native C++, FlyDSL, or LLVM source changed; native rebuild was not applicable.
